currentContext.expansion: Ruby Mills describes no named textile plant expansion with a commissioning timeline. Its stated expansion agenda is: (a) evaluation of opportunities within technical textiles as a future growth vertical; (b) a foray into solar energy initiatives to support cleaner energy adoption and mitigate operating cost pressures; (c) upgrading 'The Ruby', its Mumbai commercial tower, with modern occupier-focused infrastructure, refreshed common areas, enhanced hospitality experiences and contemporary food and beverage offerings including cafes and restaurants, alongside a leasing and monetisation mandate awarded to Gaurav Kapoor Ventures; and (d) the balance land parcel adjoining The Ruby, carrying estimated development potential of approximately over a million square feet of large-format Grade A+ commercial real estate, for which the Company is still evaluating the optimal development strategy and product mix. Beyond direct development the Company has entered a strategic investment partnership with Isprava for premium second-home and hospitality-led real estate in Alibaug, and has expanded indirect participation through 360 ONE WAM Wealth Asset Advisors alongside institutions including Blackstone and Brookfield in completed and pre-leased commercial and warehousing assets across Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai. During the year the Company obtained a renewed Occupation Certificate for The Ruby tower at Dadar including upper floors and the restaurants and food outlets, and incorporated two wholly-owned subsidiaries, Ruby Greentech K Private Limited and Ruby Greentech T Private Limited, on 18th March 2026, whose operations are yet to commence.

- MD&A states weak market sentiments and cautious procurement behaviour across markets have created a measured demand environment for the industry, directly constraining volume and pricing in the textiles division.

- MD&A opens with geopolitical tensions affecting demand patterns and closes by saying global economic and geopolitical uncertainties continue to warrant caution on the outlook.
- The real-estate division's earnings and value rest heavily on 'The Ruby' at Dadar plus the adjoining balance land parcel, so occupancy, tenant quality and Mumbai commercial-market conditions are a concentrated exposure; the Company has appointed an external advisory firm specifically to drive leasing and monetisation.
- The balance land parcel's approximately-over-a-million-square-feet potential is unrealised — the Company is still evaluating the optimal development strategy and product mix, and the existing tower required conversion from DCR 1991 to current regulations and a renewed Occupation Certificate.
- New exposures — the Isprava partnership in Alibaug second homes, indirect real-estate participation through 360 ONE WAM alongside institutional managers, technical textiles evaluation and two newly incorporated Greentech subsidiaries yet to commence operations — carry execution risk and limited direct operational control.
- The Directors' Report notes the Company's policy requires operations conducted so as to ensure safety and compliance with environmental regulations; the Board has a Risk Management Policy, though it states that at present there is no identifiable risk which in its opinion may threaten the existence of the Company.
